title: Development of performance-based endpoints for ophthalmology using digital data on smartphone use and activity (PERODI)
summary:
For common chronic eye diseases (e.g., age-related macular degeneration [AMD]; glaucoma), the patient benefit of new therapies is typically assessed based solely on clinical data. From a societal perspective, it is particularly important to focus on therapies with measurable patient benefits. Digital, patient-centered endpoints have rarely been used in ophthalmology to date. However, highly relevant endpoint domains such as reading and mobility behavior can be ideally captured using digital behavioral data. 

The project develops digital endpoints for clinical trials in ophthalmology based on smartphone usage and accelerometer data. It consists of two phases: 

1. Systematic assessment of smartphone usage behavior in patients with chronic eye diseases (Step 1: in-depth interviews; Step 2: quantitative survey)

2. Development of digital endpoints 1. from routine smartphone usage data; 2. from   
  accelerometer data. Initial validation of the developed digital endpoints (construct
  validity [disease stage], criterion validity [visual function], sensitivity to change)

Thus, the project provides innovative endpoints for use in follow-up projects.
conditions: Chronic eye diseases: AMD (H35.3), glaucoma (H40), diabetic retinopathy (H36.0)
Degeneration of macula and posterior pole

interventions.name: Patients with chronic eye diseases (including AMD/glaucoma) will be assessed once through in-depth interviews and questionnaires, and continuously over a period of one week via digital data collection (smartphone usage data and accelerometer data via a skin-adhesive sensor patch).

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Adults capable of giving informed consent (≥ 18 years of age) with 
retinal diseases (particularly diabetic 
eye diseases, retinal vein occlusion, neovascular 
AMD) or glaucoma
Exclusion criteria:
Adults with insufficient understanding of the 
German language  
Children and adolescents (< 18 years)  
Inability to participate due to an additional disability 
(e.g., severe intellectual disability)  
Other serious mental illnesses
